subject: music
source_note: Topic structure follows the AQA A-Level Music specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Appraising music
units.blurb: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650–1910 (compulsory)

topics.name: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650–1910 (compulsory)
Two further areas chosen from: Pop music; Music for media; Music for theatre; Jazz; Contemporary traditional music; Art music since 1910

connections.why: Western classical harmony and form model the conventions a brief composition draws on
Analysing classical phrasing and structure sharpens interpretation in performance
The chosen further styles supply idioms and techniques for free composition
Repertoire from the chosen optional areas often feeds performance programmes
Working to a brief builds the craft that free composition then applies without constraint
Performing builds the practical instrument knowledge that makes compositions idiomatic
The compulsory classical study gives the analytical baseline for the optional areas
